stemMd: A mobile app introduces a reminder that appears after a user has been inactive for a week. Users who open the reminder subsequently return more often than those who do not. The team attributes this to the reminder. Which question is most useful?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Do randomly selected inactive users shown the reminder return more often than comparable users not shown it?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Do returning users use a smartphone?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Is the reminder stored as text rather than an image?

options.label: D
options.textMd: Can every user spell the app’s name?

options.label: E
options.textMd: How many years ago was the app’s first icon designed?

explanationMd: Opening a reminder is itself a selected behaviour. Random exposure addresses whether the reminder causes return rather than simply identifying users already inclined to return.

distractorRationale.d: Spelling ability is not the relevant counterfactual.
distractorRationale.c: Storage format alone does not isolate a behavioural effect.
distractorRationale.e: The icon’s age is irrelevant to this comparison.
distractorRationale.b: That does not distinguish selection into opening from a causal effect.
